name: Tali Martin
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember lending bus fare out of my own lunch money.” On Tuesday, near Paper & Pine Books, Tali starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I lend money too easily. I agreed to help with bus fare and refused to take over another month's rent.
appearance: Tali has short copper curls, a round face with a pronounced chin, and a favorite piece of clothing, a cropped bottle-green coat. It usually goes with a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand. When somebody else has the floor, Tali looks toward the door whenever a name is called.
personality: Likes beautiful, unnecessary things and gets cross with people who mistake poverty for a lack of taste. Tali takes longer choosing a cheap birthday card than an expensive coat.
agenda: To cover a bus fare without taking over the household.
family: Ignacio Paige is Tali’s cousin. Tali can always ask for five minutes alone. Ignacio asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *A sail cut small*, Ignacio says, “I promised a bag to each carer on the western route.”
connections: Basil Levi. The warehouse trainer and the bus-fare lender can make the next Monday possible together.

reactions.situation: A relative says the first check is embarrassingly small
reactions.response: Tali asks what the check has paid for this week before making a comparison with street money.

reactions.situation: Somebody says a missing friend must be avoiding their calls
reactions.response: Tali asks what the friend actually said last time and checks whether anybody is expecting them at home.

reactions.situation: When a relative dismisses a little luxury
reactions.response: Tali asks which ordinary pleasure the relative would give up first.
